@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("processed", "failed", "expected"),
    [(100, 100, OperationalOutcome.FAILED),
     (100, 7, OperationalOutcome.PARTIAL),
     (100, 0, OperationalOutcome.COMPLETED),
     (0, 0, OperationalOutcome.SKIPPED)],
)
def test_batch_summary_uses_business_counters(processed, failed, expected):
    assert OperationalBatchCounts(processed, failed).outcome is expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("outcome", "level"),
    [(OperationalOutcome.COMPLETED, logging.INFO),
     (OperationalOutcome.COMPLETED_WITH_RETRIES, logging.INFO),
     (OperationalOutcome.SKIPPED, logging.INFO),
     (OperationalOutcome.BLOCKED, logging.WARNING),
     (OperationalOutcome.PARTIAL, logging.WARNING),
     (OperationalOutcome.FAILED, logging.ERROR)],
)
def test_explicit_summary_severity(caplog, outcome, level):
    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO)
    log_operational_event(logging.getLogger("outcome-regression"), OperationalLogEvent(
        name=OperationalEventName.ERP_MATERIAL_STATUS_REFRESH_COMPLETED,
        outcome=outcome, component="dotmac_erp", counters={"failed": 100},
    ))
    record = caplog.records[-1]
    assert record.levelno == level
    assert record.outcome == outcome.value


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("processed", "failed", "expected"),
    [(100, 100, "failed"), (100, 1, "partial"), (100, 0, "completed"), (0, 0, "skipped")])
def test_material_task_uses_typed_outcome_and_records_real_status(
    monkeypatch, caplog, processed, failed, expected,
):
    from app import metrics
    from app.services import observability
    from app.services.dotmac_erp import material_sync
    from app.tasks import dotmac_erp_outbox

    observation = material_sync.MaterialStatusRefreshOutcome(
        processed=processed, observed=processed-failed, updated=0,
        skipped_not_owned=0, failed=failed,
        errors=tuple("synthetic failed observation" for _ in range(failed)),
    )
    runner = MagicMock(return_value=observation)
    monkeypatch.setattr(material_sync, "run_refresh_material_request_statuses", runner)
    metric = MagicMock()
    recorded = MagicMock()
    monkeypatch.setattr(metrics, "observe_job", metric)
    monkeypatch.setattr(observability, "record_task_run", recorded)
    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO)
    result = dotmac_erp_outbox.refresh_material_request_statuses()
    assert result["operational_outcome"] == expected
    assert result["failed"] == failed
    assert result["updated"] == 0
    assert metric.call_args.args[1] == OperationalOutcome(expected).recording_status
    assert recorded.call_args.kwargs["status"] == OperationalOutcome(expected).recording_status
    assert recorded.call_args.kwargs["counters"]["failed"] == failed
    assert "errors" not in recorded.call_args.kwargs["counters"]
    runner.assert_called_once()


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("status", "skipped", "expected"), [
    ("blocked", "retry_not_due", "blocked"),
    ("blocked", None, "blocked"),
    ("retryable", "retry_not_due", "completed_with_retries"),
    ("disabled", "capability_disabled", "skipped"),
    ("already_running", "already_running", "skipped"),
    ("success", None, "completed"),
])
def test_operational_erp_summary_keeps_owner_backoff_state(
    monkeypatch, caplog, status, skipped, expected,
):
    from app.services import job_heartbeat
    from app.services.dotmac_erp import domain_sync
    from app.services.dotmac_erp.operational_contracts import OperationalSyncRunOutcome
    from app.tasks import dotmac_erp_outbox

    observation = OperationalSyncRunOutcome(
        projects=0, tickets=0, project_tasks=0, work_orders=0,
        status=status, skipped=skipped,
    )
    runner = MagicMock(return_value=observation)
    monkeypatch.setattr(domain_sync, "run_sync_operational_domains", runner)
    recorded = MagicMock()
    monkeypatch.setattr(job_heartbeat, "record_result", recorded)
    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO)
    result = dotmac_erp_outbox.sync_erp_operational_domains()
    assert result == observation.model_dump(mode="json")
    summaries = [r for r in caplog.records if r.msg == "operational_task_outcome"]
    assert summaries[-1].outcome == expected
    assert recorded.call_args.kwargs["status"] == status
    runner.assert_called_once()

def _uisp_task_environment(monkeypatch, *, acquired=True):
    from app.services.topology import uisp_sync
    from app.tasks import topology_uisp

    db = MagicMock()
    @contextmanager
    def lock(*args, **kwargs):
        yield db, acquired
    monkeypatch.setattr(topology_uisp.db_session_adapter, "advisory_lock", lock)
    monkeypatch.setattr(topology_uisp, "uisp_configured", lambda: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(topology_uisp.UispClient, "from_env", MagicMock(return_value=MagicMock()))
    stats = MagicMock()
    record = MagicMock()
    monkeypatch.setattr(topology_uisp, "store_task_stats", stats)
    monkeypatch.setattr(topology_uisp, "record_task_run", record)
    return topology_uisp, uisp_sync, db, stats, record


@pytest.mark.parametrize("failures", [{"failed": 629}, {"port_fetch_failures": 1}, {"link_fetch_failures": 1}])
def test_uisp_completed_pass_with_failures_is_partial(monkeypatch, failures):
    task, service, db, stats, recorded = _uisp_task_environment(monkeypatch)
    counters = {"created": 1, **failures}
    monkeypatch.setattr(service, "sync", MagicMock(return_value=counters))
    result = task.run_uisp_topology_sync()
    assert result == {**counters, "operational_outcome": "partial"}
    stats.assert_called_once_with("uisp_sync", counters)
    assert recorded.call_args.kwargs["status"] == "partial"
    db.commit.assert_called_once()


def test_uisp_protected_review_is_not_a_transport_failure(monkeypatch):
    task, service, db, stats, recorded = _uisp_task_environment(monkeypatch)
    counters = {"failed": 0, "onu_topology_review_required": 38, "prune_guarded": 3}
    monkeypatch.setattr(service, "sync", MagicMock(return_value=counters))
    assert task.run_uisp_topology_sync()["operational_outcome"] == "completed"
    assert recorded.call_args.kwargs["status"] == "success"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["provider", "timeout", "unexpected", "invalid_summary"])
def test_uisp_failure_outcomes_never_report_success(monkeypatch, kind):
    from billiard.exceptions import SoftTimeLimitExceeded
    task, service, db, stats, recorded = _uisp_task_environment(monkeypatch)
    if kind == "invalid_summary":
        runner = MagicMock(return_value={"failed": "not-a-number"})
    else:
        failure = {
            "provider": task.UispClientError("private provider details"),
            "timeout": SoftTimeLimitExceeded(),
            "unexpected": RuntimeError("private failure details"),
        }[kind]
        runner = MagicMock(side_effect=failure)
    monkeypatch.setattr(service, "sync", runner)
    if kind in {"unexpected", "invalid_summary"}:
        with pytest.raises((RuntimeError, TypeError)):
            task.run_uisp_topology_sync()
    else:
        result = task.run_uisp_topology_sync()
        assert result["operational_outcome"] == "failed"
        assert "private" not in str(result)
    assert recorded.call_args.kwargs["status"] == "error"
    assert "private" not in str(stats.call_args)
    db.rollback.assert_called_once()
    runner.assert_called_once()


def test_uisp_lock_skip_does_not_clobber_last_real_stats(monkeypatch):
    task, service, db, stats, recorded = _uisp_task_environment(monkeypatch, acquired=False)
    runner = MagicMock()
    monkeypatch.setattr(service, "sync", runner)
    assert task.run_uisp_topology_sync()["operational_outcome"] == "skipped"
    stats.assert_not_called()
    runner.assert_not_called()
    assert recorded.call_args.kwargs["status"] == "skipped"


def test_material_runner_retains_typed_return_until_serialization():
    import ast
    from pathlib import Path

    path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "app/services/dotmac_erp/material_sync.py"
    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
    runner = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "run_refresh_material_request_statuses")
    assert isinstance(runner.returns, ast.Name)
    assert runner.returns.id == "MaterialStatusRefreshOutcome"
    assert not any(isinstance(n, ast.Attribute) and n.attr == "as_dict" for n in ast.walk(runner))

### Integration business-outcome reporting

Material status refresh crosses the task boundary as
`MaterialStatusRefreshOutcome`, not an untyped result dictionary. The task
serializes only after interpreting attempted/failed counters through the typed
`OperationalBatchCounts` observation: all failed is `failed`, some failed is
`partial`, an empty selection is `skipped`, otherwise it is `completed`.
Unchanged successful observations still count as completed work.

ERP operational sync keeps the owner's blocked/retryable status and next-attempt
clock, including retry-not-due invocations. Per-entity errors cannot refresh a
successful-delivery heartbeat. Expected refusals and backoff are not exceptions
or permission bypasses.

UISP reports explicit transport/run failures separately from per-item/port/link
failures in a returned pass. The latter is partial, not a claim that every
phase failed. Unmatched devices, topology review and prune guards remain
protected domain outcomes, not transport failures. Unexpected exceptions stay
failed Celery tasks; no whole-batch autoretry is added because prior phases may
already have committed. Lock/configuration skips do not replace the
cached last real topology statistics. The existing cache continues to receive
its original numeric/error shape.

`completed`, `completed_with_retries`, and `skipped` summaries use INFO;
`partial` and `blocked` use WARNING; explicit `failed` uses ERROR. Material and
UISP task adapters publish their factual run result through the existing
observability recording owner and return an `operational_outcome` marker.
Framework SUCCESS cannot advance last-success freshness for these two tasks
unless that marker is exactly `completed`. Missing or unknown markers fail
closed. This opt-in contract does not reinterpret arbitrary task results.

Operator alert inputs are the `operational_task_outcome` event's event_name,
outcome, component and counters, plus the existing last-result/last-success
records and topology failure gauges. Alert on failed/partial results and aged
last success; do not use framework completion or the timestamp of the latest
failed attempt as proof of healthy delivery. This change supplies the signals;
no production alert destination or rule is changed automatically.

Regression coverage in `tests/test_structured_operational_logging.py` exercises
the typed material result, ERP backoff, severity, framework-success guard, UISP
partial/failure/skip handling and the typed material serialization boundary.
The existing topology-cache regression preserves the last-result wire format.
